    HOW IT WORKS / YOUR APPLICATION

    Your workflow.
    AI spend you can trace.

    The office shows one example. In your application, keep the agents and tools you already use and add a recording step around their calls. Your backend connects usage and cost to the customer, task and agent doing the work.

    1. 01 / CAPTURE

      Capture the work as it happens.

      Collect usage from each model or tool call. Attach customer, task and agent IDs, then calculate the charge using your own pricing rules.

    2. 02 / SIGN & STORE

      Write a signed SDK record.

      Your backend signs the usage payload, verifies the transaction and appends it to the SDK's Oracle ledger. This is the recording pattern used to create the records in this demo.

    3. 03 / USE THE DATA

      Bring the costs back into your app.

      Read the records into your dashboard. Group them by customer or task, investigate an individual call and export the data for reporting or your billing system.

    This hosted demo replays records made from sample usage and prices. Your application supplies its own usage and pricing. The signature verifies the recorder and the unchanged payload; it does not independently prove that the reported usage is true.

    What would this look like for your team?

    Bring a recurring task and the tools it calls. Walk through where to capture usage, how to attribute cost and how the records could fit into your existing workflow.

    Simulation assumptions & SDK details +

    Exactly the same assigned tasks. Both teams draw from the same continuous backlog of synthetic vendor briefs. Each uses three vendors, requirements and a supplied expected report. Work stays available throughout the shift. Staffing, processing times and the selected cutoff determine how much finishes; there is no fixed brief quota. The schedule stores the work either team can start within that time.

    Finite capacity, then human review. Each manual worker handles one brief at a time. Each agent handles one workflow at a time; finished agent work queues for a person to review. More agents can move the bottleneck to review. With zero agents, the assisted team's people work manually. Extra retries add the configured delay and sample call charges.

    Costs are scenario estimates. Human labor is allocated for every staffed minute, including idle time. Cost per completed brief divides total shift spend by completed output and includes unfinished work. Agent infrastructure and subscription costs are not modeled. Usage, prices and throughput are fixtures or editable assumptions, not measured customer results.

    Quality rules are shared. Reports must compare all three vendors, meet the feature checklist and select the cheapest eligible option. Checks run against supplied fixture reports; they do not establish live AI accuracy.

    SDK mode loading…

    Graphics. Original procedural models, shared geometry and textures, instanced skyline windows, a capped animation rate and a bounded receipt feed. Eco mode reduces resolution and turns off shadows.
